abstract: Designing machine learning (ML) experiments requires beginners to plan a methodologically sound workflow and implement it in a concrete environment. We evaluated two forms of support in two within-participant studies with 18 predominantly technically trained participants: mlguide, which provides structured, evidence- backed guidance for workflow design, and AI Sandbox, a visual no-code environment for workflow implementation. After using mlguide, participants produced better high-level workflow designs, but their scores on a quiz about specific methodological choices did not improve significantly. Compared with Google Colab, AI Sandbox received higher hedonic user experience ratings, while perceived workload and acceptance did not differ significantly. These findings suggest that different forms of interactive support help with differ- ent aspects of beginner ML experimentation. The paper contributes a reusable evaluation task with instructions, a modified dataset, and a quiz, as well as empirical evidence on structured guidance for workflow design and on the experience of implementing workflows in visual and notebook-based environments.

ur.ai_reason: 两项参与者研究评估ML实验设计工具
ur.tldr: 面向机器学习实验新手，比较结构化指导工具mlguide与可视化无代码环境AI Sandbox，并以Google Colab为参照开展18人组内研究。mlguide改善高层工作流设计，但未显著提升方法知识；Sandbox的愉悦度更高，工作量与接受度无显著差异。

title: Designing Accessible and Rigorous ML Experiments: No-Code Visual Workflows and Structured Guidance for Beginners
title_zh: 设计易用且严谨的 ML 实验：面向初学者的无代码可视化工作流与结构化指导
